expected.rationale: The original SCRAMBLER hypothesis for this hole was factually wrong and is rejected here: at 444 yards with an unrecoverable ocean cliff running the entire left side (tee to green) and severe dunes/bunkers right, this is not the short, hazard-light, recovery-rewarding hole it was assumed to be. GolfCourseGurus explicitly states the hole 'rewards aggressive shot-making and accuracy' and 'punishes timid play and wayward drives into either hazard.' Registered as a genuine BOMBER/STRAIGHT toss-up: the ~225-yard carry requirement rewards power, but neither hazard offers a scrambler-friendly recovery.
sources: The Fried Egg, 'Pacific Dunes Course Review and Rating'
Bandon Dunes Golf (official), Pacific Dunes No. 13 posting (427-444 yards)

approximations: no scoring average available (resort course, no tournament history)
the ocean cliff (left side, tee-to-green) is approximated as a series of water-creek segments; the real hazard is unrecoverable (lost ball/OB), which the sim's one-stroke water penalty understates
the 60-foot dune near the green is approximated as a scaled-up bunker
the hog's-back fairway ridge that redirects short drives right is not modeled (no ball-redirect-on-carry mechanic beyond existing roll/slope)
disagreement: Pre-registered as a BOMBER/STRAIGHT tie; observed is a STRAIGHT/TOUCH tie (margin 0.17, above TIE_EPSILON so not even a tie-match on its own terms), meaning both the archetype pair and the tie-closeness are off. Consistent with the shared root cause on augusta-13: STRAIGHT's structurally lower dispersion coefficient makes it the default winner across this entire real-hole set almost regardless of hole design, so a pre-registered BOMBER-inclusive tie was always a stretch against that pattern. TOUCH's presence as the second-place archetype (rather than BOMBER) is the more surprising part and not fully explained by the shared root cause alone -- worth a closer look if this hole's geometry is revisited, but not adjusted here since there's no scoring-average signal to confirm the encoding itself is at fault.
